input.claim_text: On 3 February 2024 a cricket ball hit by kids playing in the street smashed one of our large front windows. Glass shattered onto the living room floor but thankfully no one was hurt. I've boarded it up for now but haven't had a glazier come out to quote the replacement yet.

output.cause: cricket ball struck window during play

input.query: Is accidental breakage of glass/windows caused by an external object (e.g. thrown ball) covered?

output.answer:
Based on the provided excerpts, this appears to be covered, but with an important qualification.

Under the "Accidental glass breakage" insured event, coverage applies to breakage of glass generally, but is subject to a specific limitation: breakage is **excluded** unless "the break extends through the entire thickness of the glass" [RealInsurance Landlord PDS, page 15; RealInsurance Contents PDS, page 16]. This means that if a thrown ball caused a crack or chip that does not go all the way through the glass, it would not be covered, but if it breaks through the full thickness of the glass, it would fall within the covered event.

Additionally, the excerpts note that "we also do not pay for damage caused by the broken item" — meaning any resulting damage caused by the glass itself breaking (e.g., shards causing further damage) is excluded, unless Top cover has been taken out [RealInsurance Contents PDS, page 16].

The excerpts do not explicitly address the ball itself as the causing object, nor whether damage to the ball or other consequential circumstances would be covered — only the glass breakage event and its exclusions are detailed. There is no specific exclusion mentioned for breakage caused by external thrown objects, so based on the general terms provided, such breakage would be covered as "Accidental Glass Breakage" [RealInsurance Home KFS, page 1; RealInsurance Contents KFS, page 1], provided it breaks through the entire thickness of the glass and is not one of the excluded glass types (e.g., glasshouse, greenhouse, conservatory, stove top, cooking surface, heater, oven door, computer/TV screens) [RealInsurance Landlord PDS, page 15; RealInsurance Contents PDS, page 16].

**Summary:** Yes, breakage of glass/windows from an external object like a thrown ball would generally be covered under "Accidental Glass Breakage," provided the break goes through the full thickness of the glass and the glass is not one of the specifically excluded types [RealInsurance Landlord PDS, page 15; RealInsurance Contents PDS, page 16; RealInsurance Home KFS, page 1; RealInsurance Contents KFS, page 1]. The excerpts do not provide further detail on scenarios involving the causing object itself.
